title: Recursive characterization of canonical integral realization
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. On the small pro-etale sites of finite-type $k$-schemes use the strict semilinear system categories $\mathscr S_W$, reduction $\mathcal R_W$, total limit $\mathcal L_W$, and actual adjunction unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Use the operations $P_v,S_p,J_j,\otimes^L$ and their integral counterparts from [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization], with $v$ separated finite type, $p$ proper and $j$ quasi-compact open. Restrict all input and intermediate systems to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals; integral inputs are derived complete and constructible. Let $d_A$ be exactly the single-operation identification of [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence], including its specified localized open comparison. On these domains $u_K$ and $e_M$ are invertible. The canonical realization comparisons $c_V$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] are characterized by the following identities. For a variable, $c_{K_i}=u_{K_i}^{-1}$. For a unary basic operation set
$$a_A(M)=d_A(\mathcal L M)\circ(\mathcal L A(e_M))^{-1}:\mathcal L A(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\rm int}(\mathcal L M).$$
For tensor set
$$a_\otimes(M,N)=d_\otimes(\mathcal L M,\mathcal L N)\circ\bigl(\mathcal L(e_M\otimes^L e_N)\bigr)^{-1}:\mathcal L(M\otimes^L N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L M\widehat\otimes^L\mathcal L N.$$
For $M=V(\mathcal R K_i)$ and $N=T(\mathcal R K_i)$, with independent leaf slots, the identities are
$$c_{AV}=A_{\rm int}(c_V)\circ a_A(M),\qquad c_{V\otimes T}=(c_V\widehat\otimes^Lc_T)\circ a_\otimes(M,N).$$
All these identities are natural in the input morphisms. This characterizes the specified comparisons themselves, including their normalization at a variable; it asserts no compatibility with shifts.

proof.text: For a normalized system $M$, [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] says that the canonical counit comparisons $(\mathcal LM)\otimes^L_R A_n\to M_n$ are isomorphisms and that $\mathcal LM$ is derived complete. These are precisely the evaluations of the actual $e_M$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The latter statement detects isomorphisms by derived evaluations, so $e_M$ is invertible in $D(\mathscr S_W)$. This is detection of isomorphisms, with no assertion about detecting equality. Its evaluated isomorphisms identify the reductions of $\mathcal LM$ with the levels of $M$, so they also give constructibility and exactly the assumed common cohomological and Tor bounds. Thus every use of $d_A(\mathcal LM)$ below has the stipulated integral input and normalized-system hypotheses.

proof.text: The right triangle identity from [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] gives $\mathcal L(e_M)u_{\mathcal LM}=1$, hence $u_{\mathcal LM}=\mathcal L(e_M)^{-1}$. For an allowed integral $K$, its reduction $\mathcal RK$ is one of the normalized input systems in the hypotheses. The variable-expression case of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] supplies an isomorphism $h:\mathcal L\mathcal RK\to K$. Only existence of this isomorphism is used here, not its normalization. Naturality gives $u_Kh=\mathcal L\mathcal R(h)u_{\mathcal L\mathcal RK}$. All factors on the right and $h$ are invertible, so the specified actual unit $u_K$ is invertible. This avoids identifying an arbitrary Roos-triangle lift with the actual unit.

proof.text:
Write $I_V=V_{\rm int}(K_i)$ and $M_V=V(\mathcal RK_i)$. Unpack the coefficient construction of the specified realization: at a variable its coefficient map is $q_{K_i}=1_{\mathcal RK_i}$; at a unary or tensor node it is the successive composite of the canonical single-operation coefficient maps:
$$q_{AV}=A(q_V)r_A(I_V),\qquad q_{V\otimes T}=(q_V\otimes^Lq_T)r_\otimes(I_V,I_T).$$
These are definitions of the composite comparison, not a claim that finite evaluations determine it. The single-operation maps are the actual system maps $r_A=e_{A\mathcal RI}\mathcal R(d_A(I)^{-1})$ of [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence], with its specified localized open comparison. Under the adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] the transpose of $q_V:\mathcal RI_V\to M_V$ is
$$b_V=\mathcal L(q_V)u_{I_V}:I_V\to\mathcal LM_V,$$
and the inverse transposition formula is $q_V=e_{M_V}\mathcal R(b_V)$. Indeed substitution reduces this equality to naturality of $e$ and $e_{\mathcal RI_V}\mathcal R(u_{I_V})=1$. At a single operation the transpose is $d_A(I)^{-1}$: substitute the displayed $r_A$, move $\mathcal R(d_A^{-1})$ past the unit, and cancel $\mathcal L(e_N)u_{\mathcal LN}=1$ for $N=A\mathcal RI$. This fixes the basic normalization, including $J_j$. At a leaf $b_{K_i}=u_{K_i}$, so the realized comparison there is $b_{K_i}^{-1}=u_{K_i}^{-1}$.

proof.text:
Suppose the inverse comparison $b_V:I_V\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal LM$ has been constructed for a smaller tree, with $M=M_V$. Transpose the unary coefficient composite in step 3. The single-operation transpose calculated there first gives
$$b_{AV}=\mathcal LA(q_V)d_A(I_V)^{-1}.$$
Substitute $q_V=e_M\mathcal R(b_V)$ and then use naturality of $d_A$ at $b_V$ to obtain
$$b_{AV}=\mathcal LA(e_M)\,d_A(\mathcal LM)^{-1}\,A_{\rm int}(b_V).$$
Each factor is invertible, by steps 1-2 and the stipulated single-operation isomorphism. Inverting this equality, in reverse order, gives
$$b_{AV}^{-1}=A_{\rm int}(b_V^{-1})\,d_A(\mathcal LM)\bigl(\mathcal LA(e_M)\bigr)^{-1}.$$
The last two factors are exactly $a_A(M)$ in the statement. The common bounds and compatible origin witnesses are those explicitly required of this intermediate system; $I_V\cong\mathcal LM$ also ensures that $d_A(I_V)$ is used on a complete constructible input. This calculation treats each of $P_v,S_p,J_j$ with its own prescribed $d_A$, without substituting a different open-extension comparison.

proof.text:
For two smaller trees write $M=M_V$, $N=M_T$ and use their independent input slots. Transposing their binary coefficient composite gives
$$b_{V\otimes T}=\mathcal L(q_V\otimes^Lq_T)d_\otimes(I_V,I_T)^{-1}.$$
Substitute $q_V=e_M\mathcal R(b_V)$ and $q_T=e_N\mathcal R(b_T)$. Bifunctoriality factors their tensor into $(e_M\otimes^Le_N)(\mathcal R(b_V)\otimes^L\mathcal R(b_T))$. Naturality of the two-input $d_\otimes$ then gives
$$b_{V\otimes T}=\mathcal L(e_M\otimes^Le_N)d_\otimes(\mathcal LM,\mathcal LN)^{-1}(b_V\widehat\otimes^Lb_T).$$
Every factor is invertible; in particular tensor sends the inverses of $e_M,e_N$ to the inverse of their tensor. Invert this identity to get
$$b_{V\otimes T}^{-1}=(b_V^{-1}\widehat\otimes^Lb_T^{-1})d_\otimes(\mathcal LM,\mathcal LN)\bigl(\mathcal L(e_M\otimes^Le_N)\bigr)^{-1}.$$
This is precisely the claimed tensor recursion with $a_\otimes(M,N)$. All tensors in the system calculation are over the ring system $((A_n)_W)_n$; the tensor on integral objects is the completed tensor specified by $d_\otimes$.

proof.text: Induct on the number of operation vertices in the finite well-typed tree. The variable case is step 3, the unary step is step 4, and the binary step is step 5; both immediate subtrees have fewer vertices. These steps construct invertible $b_V$ on exactly the assumed domains. The canonical reduction/limit transport is $c_V=b_V^{-1}$: step 3 starts with the identity comparison of the reduction of a variable, substitutes the prescribed basic coefficient maps, and takes their adjunction transpose. This also agrees directly with the specified construction in [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]: inserting $e_M^{-1}:M\to\mathcal R\mathcal LM$ before a basic $d_A$ gives exactly the last two factors of step 4, and inserting $e_M^{-1}\otimes^Le_N^{-1}$ gives those of step 5. Thus the calculation identifies the specified comparisons themselves. It does not infer their normalization merely from the existence or generator-intertwining assertion of that node. Finally any other family satisfying the displayed identities equals this one: equality holds at variables, and at a unary or tensor node the fixed $a_A$ or $a_\otimes$ and the induction equalities of the children give equality at that node. This proves the characterization without moving any clause into a new lemma.

proof.text:
The recursion is natural on the specified input domains. For a system map $f:M\to M'$, counit naturality says $f e_M=e_{M'}\mathcal R\mathcal L(f)$. Apply $\mathcal LA$ and solve for the inverse factors to get
$$\bigl(\mathcal LA(e_{M'})\bigr)^{-1}\mathcal LA(f)=\mathcal LA\mathcal R\mathcal L(f)\bigl(\mathcal LA(e_M)\bigr)^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $d_A$ now yields $a_A(M')\mathcal LA(f)=A_{\rm int}(\mathcal Lf)a_A(M)$. For maps $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$, tensor the two counit equations and apply the same calculation with the two-input $d_\otimes$; it yields
$$a_\otimes(M',N')\mathcal L(f\otimes^Lg)=(\mathcal Lf\widehat\otimes^L\mathcal Lg)a_\otimes(M,N).$$
The inverse-unit leaf comparison is natural because $u$ is natural. Paste these unary and binary squares with the induction squares for the children. This proves naturality of every $c_V$ in all independent leaf slots. A zero input and an empty open give the unique maps on zero objects; a single leaf gives the actual inverse unit, rather than an arbitrary automorphism of its limit. At a point with $K=R[0]$, a one-operation expression specializes to its specified $d_A$ by the triangle calculation in step 3. No level $n=0$ or shift compatibility is used.
